2f9efeb6874b73c3: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 181 undocumented migrants were arrested during an Immigration Department raid at Pasar Raja Bot, Chow Kit.
The operation, which began at 9.40am, involved about 200 Immigration officers and personnel who surrounded the area, a popular spot among foreigners, particularly Indonesians.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said 512 people were checked during Ops Mega Bersepadu.
Those arrested included 106 Indonesian men and 41 women and children.
The others comprised 20 Bangladeshi men, three Indian men, five Nepali men, one Pakistani man and five people of other nationalities, including a child.
The 181 detainees comprised 136 men and 45 women, aged between 10 and 55. They were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot.
Lokman said the location was among 224 hotspots nationwide frequented by undocumented migrants, particularly Indonesians.

The integrated operation involved 264 officers and personnel from the Immigration Department, Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the National Registration Department, the Fire and Rescue Department and the police.
"Foreigners used various methods to avoid arrest, including hiding on rooftops, but the use of drones enabled them to be detected," he said at a press conference.
Chow Kit is a busy commercial area in central Kuala Lumpur, known for its wet market, wholesale trade and large migrant community.
c4847b9309dd62fe: Their most pressing challenge is solving the long-standing water shortage in the village
Originally published on Global Voices
Participants of the project in Qyzylsay, Kazakhstan. Photo by Nazgul Aidabossynova. Used with permission.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

Women in the rural areas of Kazakhstan are among those most affected by climate change, energy deficit, and poor governance. They bear the heavy burden of water shortages, especially in the southern parts of the country, where this problem is the most acute due to dense population, economic reliance on agriculture, and water losses related to outdated irrigation infrastructure.

In the village of Qyzylsay, located in the southern Jambyl region, the water shortage has become a major issue affecting the daily lives of women. It forces them to spend multiple hours a day outside their homes to secure water for their households, gardens, and animals. Their grueling work often goes unnoticed and unpaid, and their geographical remoteness places limits on access to information and government services, exacerbating their situation.

In 2026, Nazgul Aidabossynova, a local activist, implemented a project to help local women improve their livelihoods by training them to engage with the government more effectively and efficiently, calculate the cost of their labor and products, and mobilize collective efforts to solve community problems. Global Voices conducted an email interview with Aidabossynova to learn more about her initiative. The interview has been edited for clarity and brevity.
Global Voices (GV): Please tell us about your organization and why you chose to get involved with the Digital Sparks project.

Nazgul Aidabossynova (NA): I represent a community-based initiative led by rural women in Qyzylsay. Our work focuses on supporting women who manage households, small farms, livestock, and care responsibilities, while also facing limited access to information, public services, and opportunities for civic participation.

We chose to participate in the Digital Sparks project because digital tools can make a direct, practical difference in women’s daily lives. Many women already own smartphones, but previously used them mainly for calls and WhatsApp.

The project created an opportunity to turn these devices into tools for accessing eGov services, documenting community problems, managing farm and household responsibilities, protecting digital security, and communicating with local authorities.
GV: What issue/challenge in your community prompted you to undertake this project?

NA: The key challenge is unreliable access to water in Qyzylsay. Water often disappears from the pipes during the day, particularly in summer. This affects gardens, livestock, household work, and the health and well-being of families.

The burden falls disproportionately on women. They wake early to store water, carry water for household and agricultural needs, care for the livestock, and wait for irrigation turns. Much of this work is unpaid, time-consuming, and rarely recognized.

Women also faced barriers in reporting water problems: they knew what was happening, but often lacked the knowledge, evidence, and confidence needed to raise concerns effectively with local institutions.
GV: What are the key changes/activities that your organization implemented during your participation in the project?
NA: The project delivered four practical training sessions for ten rural women.

The first one, titled “Your Phone is More Than WhatsApp: Smartphone as Your Household Assistant”, taught them how to use smartphone reminders, photo-diaries for farm and livestock work, eGov services, strong passwords, and basic digital-security practices.

In the second workshop, titled “Smart Water: When Your Garden Tells You It’s Thirsty”, participants learned about water rights, the responsibilities of relevant local authorities, and water-supply mapping using timestamped and GPS-tagged photographs.

The third session, titled “Numbers Don’t Lie: When You Count Everything, You Earn More”, covered how to track unpaid work and calculate the real cost of agricultural products such as milk. It also discussed the economic value of time saved through smart irrigation.

In “Honest Agreement: When Technology Helps Us Trust Each Other”, the fourth and final session, participants prepared time-to-income plans, mapped local support networks, discussed peer mentoring, and agreed to begin work toward a cooperative approach to water advocacy and shared smart-irrigation infrastructure.
GV: How did your participation in the project impact your organization’s beneficiaries and the community that you serve? Please provide examples.
NA: The project helped participating women see smartphones as tools for independence, civic participation, and practical problem-solving, rather than only communication devices.
For example, women learned that they can use eGov services to request certain official documents online, reducing the need to spend time and money traveling to administrative offices.

They also learned to create structured evidence of water problems. A photograph of a dry canal, broken pipe, or contaminated water source becomes more useful for advocacy when it includes the date, location, and a written description.

The training on unpaid labor and production costs was especially meaningful. Participants calculated the value of their time and better understood the real cost of milk production and irrigation work. The discussion showed that manual irrigation may take up to 60 hours per month.
This helped participants recognize that their time has economic value, and that shared smart-irrigation solutions could create more time for income, education, rest, and community participation.
The group also began a peer-learning process. Three participants started sharing the knowledge gained during the training with neighboring women.
GV: How has your own knowledge, awareness, and experience with digital democracy and civic space changed, thanks to your participation in the project?
NA: My understanding of digital democracy has become much more practical. Before this project, digital tools could be viewed mainly as a way to communicate or access information.
Through Digital Sparks, I saw how digital tools can strengthen people’s ability to exercise rights, access public services, collect evidence, engage with local authorities, and organize collectively.
I also gained a stronger understanding of the link between digital inclusion, women’s unpaid labor, climate-related water challenges, and civic space.

For rural women, digital capacity is not only about technical skills. It is about having a voice, being able to document problems, understanding their rights, and participating in decisions that affect their families and community.
GV: What are the most valuable lessons and experiences you are taking away from this project?

NA: The most valuable lesson is that digital literacy has the greatest impact when it is directly connected to people’s real, daily needs. In Qyzylsay, water shortages, agricultural work, unpaid care responsibilities, and access to public services were the issues that made digital tools relevant and useful.

Another important lesson is that women need not only information, but also confidence and collective support. When participants understood their rights, calculated the value of their labor, and learned how to create reliable evidence, they became more prepared to speak with local authorities and work together.
The project also showed the value of peer learning. Participants are more likely to trust and learn from women in their own community who face similar challenges.
GV: What comes next? How will you apply the learning and digital capacity you have built in your future work and within your community?
NA: We will continue the peer cascade model, with trained participants sharing basic smartphone, eGov, digital safety, and evidence documentation skills with other women in Qyzylsay.

The group intends to develop a cooperative approach to the village’s water challenges. The planned cooperative would support joint advocacy, shared learning, and exploration of funding opportunities for smart-well or shared irrigation infrastructure.

In future work, we will continue combining digital skills with women’s economic empowerment, rights awareness, and local civic participation, so that rural women’s work, knowledge, and needs become more visible.
Written by Nurbek Bekmurzaev

04585cb9b3e90723: PASIR MAS: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was visibly moved as he recalled his close relationship with the late founder of Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah, Abdullah Abdul Rahman, during a gathering with about 200 congregants tonight.

Anwar spent more than 10 minutes sharing his personal experiences and memories of the late religious scholar, whom he said had played an important role in encouraging and strengthening his resolve more than 20 years ago.
Anwar said he was deeply touched by his visit to the religious institution today as he continued to hold the late Abdullah in high regard and had always prayed for him.
"Although circumstances have changed and my position has changed, I will not change.
"When I visited this madrasah more than 20 years ago, the late Abdullah gave me a lot of advice, encouragement and confidence in myself," he said.
Anwar said although the late Abdullah was known for being strict in his teaching, he had always been generous in offering advice and support.
He said the late scholar's encouragement had left a lasting impression on him, particularly during challenging periods of his life.
"That is why I felt deeply touched when I arrived here earlier. I remembered how a great religious scholar had supported me and contributed so much to my journey," he said.

Anwar said he hoped the legacy and struggles of the late Abdullah would continue to be upheld and elevated, particularly through efforts to strengthen the role of pondok institutions and Islamic education.
The Prime Minister is on a one day visit to Kelantan today.
5db9dcf07db5a135: KUALA LUMPUR: Sabah beat Terengganu 2-0 in a stormy Super League clash at Likas Stadium in Kota Kinabalu, with the visitors reduced to 10 men after Romel Morales was sent off following a VAR review on Saturday.

The flashpoint came in the closing minutes of the first half when Morales was involved in a physical altercation with several Sabah players, including bringing goalkeeper Juan Flere to the ground in an incident that left the custodian in pain.
Referee Tuan Yaasin Tuan Hanafiah reviewed the incident on VAR before showing Malaysian international Morales a straight red card, leaving Terengganu a man short for the remainder of the match.
Sabah had already established a two-goal lead through Enrique Lopez Fernandez in the 19th minute and Gonzalo Ignacio Di Renzo five minutes later.
Fernandez opened the scoring after a defensive lapse by Terengganu, with goalkeeper Suhaimi Husin unable to deal with a ball played from the middle of the pitch.
Suhaimi rushed off his line in an attempt to stop the danger but failed to reach the ball, which bounced towards the unguarded goal.
Di Renzo then doubled Sabah's advantage in the 24th minute, putting the hosts firmly in control before the half-time incident further complicated Terengganu's task.
Sabah, however, failed to capitalise on their numerical advantage after the break, with Terengganu holding firm despite playing with 10 men.
The hosts created several chances to extend their lead but were unable to find a way past a resolute Terengganu defence.
The visitors also adopted a more aggressive approach in the second half in search of a way back into the game, but could not find a goal as Sabah held on for all three points.
The match, scheduled to kick off at 5pm, was delayed by about 30 minutes due to heavy rain in Kota Kinabalu.
The victory gives Sabah three points in their bid to improve their league position, while Terengganu remain without a win after suffering another defeat.

857a7be1bba29e0b: HANOI: Hanoi will provide a one-off payment of 4 million VND (US$154) to women who give birth to two children before the age of 35 from 2027, under a policy approved by the city's People's Council, Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported.
To qualify, the women must have been registered as permanent or temporary residents of the capital for at least six months.
Under Decree No. 168/2026/ND-CP, eligibility is based on the total number of children a woman has given birth to, regardless of the number of deliveries.
A woman's age will be calculated at the time of childbirth, rather than when the birth is registered, in accordance with relevant civil and legal regulations.
Hanoi’s fertility rate has remained below the replacement level in recent years, according to the municipal People's Committee.
The total fertility rate stood at 1.88 children per woman in 2023, 1.86 in 2024 and 1.87 in 2025.
The city faces mounting pressure from rising housing, childcare and education costs, as well as the challenges of balancing work and family life, the committee said.
It said prolonged low fertility could affect Hanoi's population size and structure, accelerate population ageing and put pressure on the labour force in the long term.
The policy is intended to encourage couples to have two children and gradually bring the city's fertility rate back to the replacement level, the committee said.

Authorities also cited health considerations, noting that fertility declines with age and that pregnancies after 35 carry higher risks of complications, including high blood pressure and gestational diabetes, as well as an increased risk of certain congenital conditions.
The city estimates that about 15,000 women will qualify for the payment each year, requiring an annual budget of around 60 billion VND (US$2.33 million).

Total spending on population-related policies in 2027 is projected at 245.9 billion VND (US$9.53 million), including higher allowances for 8,500 population collaborators and support for premarital counselling and health checks.
The 4 million VND payment is intended as partial financial assistance for families raising children, rather than full compensation for childcare and education costs, the committee said.

Karnival anjuran Perpustakaan Negara Malaysia (PNM) dengan kerjasama Perbadanan Perpustakaan Awam Melaka (Perpustam) ini berlangsung selama empat hari bermula 29 Okt hingga 1 Nov. Ia menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 35,000 pengunjung.

Sepanjang karnival berlangsung, PNM turut menganjurkan Pertandingan Ruang Bacaan Keluarga Peringkat Kebangsaan 2026 yang menerima 336 penyertaan dari seluruh negara. Program Penarafan Bintang Perpustakaan Khusus Guna Sama (PKG) turut mendapat sambutan dengan penyertaan 84 perpustakaan.
Selain pameran dan jualan buku, karnival itu menampilkan pelbagai aktiviti termasuk Bicara Inspirasi, Bengkel Penulisan Kreatif dan Jejak Cop Literasi.
Menurut Aaron, karnival ini menarik penyertaan masyarakat dalam aktiviti membaca menggunakan pendekatan yang lebih inklusif dan santai.

Pengunjung yang ditemui berpandangan buku memiliki kelebihan tersendiri berbanding telefon pintar. Seorang guru tabika, Suhaida Afindi, 30, berkata aktiviti membaca melibatkan ibu bapa dan anak-anak membuka ruang komunikasi yang lebih erat, sambil membantu perkembangan bahasa dan imaginasi kanak-kanak.
Tegasnya, buku fizikal masih penting dalam memupuk minat membaca kanak-kanak dan mengeratkan hubungan antara ibu bapa dengan anak.

"Sekarang ini, banyak perkataan yang kurang baik digunakan oleh kanak-kanak. Jadi, melalui pembacaan dan komunikasi bersama ibu bapa, mereka boleh mempelajari penggunaan perkataan yang lebih baik," katanya.

Ahmad Syahir Hakim Zulkifli, 36, berpendapat buku fizikal membolehkan seseorang lebih fokus kepada pembacaan. "Kalau membaca secara dalam talian, kadangkala perhatian terganggu dengan media sosial atau aplikasi lain," katanya.
Bagi sekumpulan pelajar sekolah menengah pula, minat membaca menjadi sebahagian daripada kehidupan dengan bahan bacaan yang pelbagai.
Muhammad Zharif Naufal Salehuddin, 14, yang minat membaca sejak berusia enam tahun, mampu menghabiskan sehingga dua buku sehari bergantung pada kelapangan masa.
Katanya, bahan bacaan menambah pengetahuan dan membantu meluaskan pemikiran dan meningkatkan kefahaman terhadap sesuatu perkara.
Muhammad Darwish Aqasha Abdullah, 13, pula berkata pembaca perlu lebih berhati-hati apabila membaca di media sosial, dengan menyemak kesahihan fakta bagi mengelakkan penyebaran berita palsu.

"Perkara ini sangat berbahaya kerana saya takut generasi akan datang menganggap maklumat yang tidak benar sebagai fakta sehingga mereka tidak lagi dapat membezakan perkara yang betul atau palsu," katanya.
5dfad9996b9f2906: KOTA BARU: The Federal Government will increase grants under the Skim Usahawan Bangkit by RM200 million next year to help small entrepreneurs expand their businesses and boost their earnings.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said even modest allocations could make a significant difference when channelled directly to businesses in need.
He said relatively small purchases, such as affordable refrigerators to preserve stock, could prevent losses and generate thousands of ringgit in additional monthly income.
"Sometimes the expenditure is only RM5,000, RM3,000 or even RM1,800, but it can bring good returns.
"I have seen businesses that simply need a small, inexpensive refrigerator to keep their goods from spoiling. That alone can increase their returns by thousands of ringgit a month," he said.
Anwar was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here yesterday.
He said the government would continue monitoring the needs of entrepreneurs and provide assistance wherever possible.
He also thanked Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and the state government for their cooperation, saying any issues could be resolved through discussion.
"If there are problems, we will discuss them amicably," he said.
d43cd21daec06d55: PETALING JAYA: The trade group of private dentists has called for health minister Dzulkefly Ahmad to intervene in the enforcement of a health ministry regulation setting out minimum widths of staircases for clinics situated on the first floor or upper floors of commercial buildings.

The regulation sets a minimum staircase width of 1.1m from the handrail to the wall on existing dental clinics. The Malaysian Private Dental Practitioners' Association said it applies not only to first-floor dental clinics but also to all other private clinics situated on upper floors.

The association said an evacuation drill had demonstrated that a patient could be safely evacuated from a first-floor dental chair to a waiting ambulance despite the staircase width being less than stipulated in the regulation.
The association accused the ministry's private medical practice control section of adopting the rule without sufficiently considering the structural limitations of older commercial buildings.

The association questioned why the regulation was being "unilaterally imposed" by the health ministry as building structural compliance and fire safety requirements were the responsibilities of local authorities and the relevant fire, rescue and safety authorities.
It said regulations must be implemented "with fairness and sound consideration of the circumstances surrounding existing premises".

ca48b4aa71b156f5: PETALING JAYA: Sarawak akan terus menuntut kawalan lebih besar ke atas sumber strategiknya, termasuk industri minyak dan gas, kata Premier Abang Johari Openg.
Memetik pengambilalihan Pelabuhan Bintulu dan pelaburan Sarawak dalam Affin Bank sebagai contoh, Abang Johari berkata, masih banyak lagi aset yang ingin diambil alih oleh negeri itu.

db311b9492ec0a56: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan via Pakistan, US media reported Friday, a move advocacy groups say could endanger their lives.

Trump last year issued travel bans for a number of countries, including Afghanistan, as part of a broad immigration crackdown, and sought to end deportation protections for Afghans, some of whom were granted special immigrant visas following the August 2021 takeover by Taliban authorities.
More than 150 Afghan immigrants are expected to be deported in the latest push, The New York Times reported, citing three unnamed US officials, and the first flight could leave as soon as Monday.

Among those expected to be deported are relatives of Afghans who assisted the US military in the country prior to the fall of Kabul, according to AfghanEvac, a group seeking to help former Afghan allies.
While the US cannot arrange deportations directly to Afghanistan, the officials told the Times that Pakistan will oversee their expulsion to Afghanistan.

Pakistan's government earlier this year ordered law enforcement nationwide to arrest Afghan citizens without visas as part of a years-long repatriation policy that has pushed back millions of Afghans who fled their homes after the Taliban returned to power.

Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been fraught since the Taliban authorities took power in 2021 and worsened after deadly border clashes last October that led to near-total closure of the border.
Clashes subsided after mediation, but the conflict intensified again in February, with Pakistan declaring "an open war" on its neighbour.
Pakistan accuses Afghanistan of harbouring militants responsible for deadly attacks on its territory, an allegation the Taliban government in Afghanistan denies.
Taliban authorities were not immediately available for comment. The US department of homeland security did not respond to questions from AFP.

"America is about to put Afghans on a plane to the Taliban, and the administration is doing it the week the country goes to vote, hoping no one is watching," AfghanEvac president Shawn VanDiver said in a statement, referring to the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
VanDiver said some of the migrants facing removal "are the brothers and sons of men who served alongside US forces, families the Taliban already has every reason to target."
"Whatever path brought them here, the danger waiting for them is the same."
After regaining power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments.
However, the UN has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses.

98731a2cf16211a4: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Education (MOE) to take firm action against bullying in schools amid growing concerns over children’s safety and well-being.
He said cases involving children, including suicide, abuse and bullying, highlighted the need to strengthen character development and moral values from an early age.
Anwar said academic excellence alone was insufficient, stressing that education must also instil good manners, respect and a sense of responsibility among students.
“Bullying and humiliating others show that there are still shortcomings in instilling values and proper conduct in our education system.

“The Education Ministry has been directed to be firm and take decisive action. Teachers and educators must also help look after our children,” he said at the launch of the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.
Anwar also stressed the importance of religious education, including understanding and practising the teachings of the Quran, performing prayers and respecting parents, teachers and peers.

a099a296af9f9f42: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — The government is considering Perak as the venue for the launch of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) master plan, which could coincide with the two countries’ Annual Leaders’ Retreat scheduled to be held in the state on December 4.

Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said it had been agreed that the launch would be witnessed jointly by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart, Lawrence Wong.
“Both prime ministers have agreed to witness the launch of the master plan. We are now finalising the venue, as this year’s Annual Leaders’ Retreat is expected to be held in Ipoh.

“We are considering whether the launch will take place there or whether other arrangements will be made. However, both prime ministers have agreed to witness the ceremony,” he told a press conference after the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency’s Deepavali celebration in Larkin here today.
On preparations for Monday’s bilateral meeting in Singapore, Akmal Nasrullah said Singapore would host the meeting.
He described the meeting as significant as it would be the first to be held under the Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee framework.
He is scheduled to lead the Malaysian delegation alongside Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi, while Singapore’s delegation will be led by National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat.
“From Malaysia’s perspective, this meeting presents an opportunity to assess progress in implementing the JS-SEZ initiative and discuss plans for the way forward,” he said.
Akmal Nasrullah said the programme framework and logistical arrangements for the Annual Leaders’ Retreat were being refined to maximise its impact following the launch of the master plan.
On the Deepavali celebration, he said a total of RM318,000 had been allocated to improve community well-being in the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency.
He presented RM260,000 under the Prime Minister’s Office’s Madani Infrastructure and Social Response Programme (PRISMA) for repairs to staircase handrails at Rumah Pangsa Serantau Baru in Larkin.
He said the infrastructure improvements were aimed at enhancing residents’ safety and comfort, particularly for senior citizens, children and other vulnerable groups.

A further RM47,500 was allocated to upgrade places of worship serving the Indian community, while RM10,500 was distributed among four local non-governmental organisations to support welfare, cultural and community development programmes. — Bernama
641caa4e2bf968e5: BEIRUT: The Israeli army carried out fresh airstrikes, an explosion and machine-gun fire across southern Lebanon early Saturday, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported, citing Lebanon's state-run National News Agency.
The attacks came despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed by Lebanon and Israel in June and renewed diplomatic efforts to address security disputes between the two sides.
Israeli strikes and military operations targeted several locations across southern Lebanon, including the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun, according to the news agency.
In the Nabatieh district, Israeli warplanes struck an area between the towns of Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Kfar Tebnit.
Another Israeli airstrike targeted the outskirts of Baraachit in the Bint Jbeil district, the agency said.
In Marjayoun district, Israeli forces carried out an explosion in the town of Tallousa, while a drone flew at low altitude over nearby towns, according to the report.
It said that Israeli forces also opened machine-gun fire from the direction of Khiam toward agricultural land in Ibl al-Saqi.
Israeli warplanes separately struck an area between the towns of Adshit al-Qusayr and Taybeh.
In the Tyre district, Israeli drones flew at low altitude over the city of Tyre and surrounding towns, reaching both banks of the Litani River in the Qasmiyeh area.
According to an Anadolu correspondent, Israeli drones have continued flying over Beirut’s southern suburbs since the morning.
The latest Israeli attacks followed US-sponsored military and technical talks between Lebanon and Israel in Tampa, Florida, on Oct 20 to 21.
The meetings ended without an announced breakthrough or a joint statement.
Reports indicated that the sides agreed to continue negotiations, although disagreements remained over Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon and the disarmament of Hezbollah.
The June framework agreement provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territories in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army and the disarmament of armed groups.
Despite the agreement, Israel has continued military operations in Lebanon.
Since March 2, the attacks have killed at least 4,386 people, wounded 12,407 others and displaced more than one million people, according to the Lebanese health ministry.
7c85712d0ec20d1e: SHAH ALAM: Chicken suspected of having been killed by electric current before slaughter at a processing plant raided in Puchong yesterday may have been supplied to Muslim-owned restaurants.

Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary investigations found that the premises used the water-bath stunning method, with excessively high electric voltage believed to have caused the chickens to die before slaughter.
He said the council was concerned that the chicken supply had reached Muslim-owned restaurants.
"How can we allow these irresponsible people to do such a thing?" he said.
He urged Muslims, restaurant operators and food business owners to check the source of their chicken supplies and ensure that the food they serve is halal.

"If they (restaurants) do not care where their chicken supplies come from, (I am worried) this will cause Muslims to consume non-halal food," he said after the Selangor State-Level 2026 Ahlus Sunnah Wal Jamaah Fundamental Declaration programme.
Salehuddin said preliminary investigations found that the premises were believed to be Muslim-owned and had been operating for a long time.

He said the premises had been ordered to close for two weeks to facilitate investigations, adding that Mais, through the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), would continue conducting integrated operations with other government agencies.
More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering and halal certification requirements were seized during the raid.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men believed to be involved in the slaughtering and processing activities were also detained during Ops Taring Chiller.
The operation involved the police, Jais, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), the Department of Environment and the Petaling Health Office.

Under Islamic slaughtering requirements, chickens must be alive at the time of slaughter, with a sharp knife used to sever the throat and major blood vessels. Electrical stunning is permitted under halal standards only if it does not kill the poultry before slaughter.
be4367d2c7821e57: SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today launched the National Courier Day 2026 (HKN2026) celebration, recognising the industry’s RM6.9 billion contribution to the country’s digital economy, at the Selangor International Trade Centre.

Themed “Sustaining the Industry, Strengthening Trust,” the event was organised by the Malaysian Express Carriers Association (AMEC) with support from the Communications Ministry through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).

MCMC said the government remains committed to strengthening the postal and courier industry through regulatory reform, strategic cooperation and digital transformation to improve service efficiency, industry competitiveness and consumer safety.

“On regulatory reform, the government is reviewing proposed amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012 (Act 741) and plans to gazette the Postal Services Regulations (Postal Service Security and Prohibited Postal Articles) 2026 (PSR2026), subject to the relevant approval process.
“These measures aim to strengthen security, industry accountability and consumer protection, in step with the rapid growth of e-commerce,” MCMC said in a statement today.

Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali, AMEC chairman Ronald Tan, and representatives of government agencies, postal and courier industry players.
Parcel Shield, an initiative led by the Postal Forum with MCMC support, was also launched at HKN2026 to tackle parcel delivery fraud.

“The initiative, among others, encourages information sharing between courier companies and e-commerce platforms, and the dissemination of fraud alerts to enhance consumer protection and confidence,” the statement read.
HKN2026 further saw the signing of a memorandum of collaboration for the Courier Network Sharing initiative, a last-mile delivery pilot at selected locations.
“The project will assess the potential for infrastructure optimisation, reduced operational overlap and improved service access before expansion is considered,” the statement read.

Additionally, digital transformation is being strengthened through the National Address System (NAS) to improve address accuracy and delivery efficiency, and PAKEJ Map, which helps users locate more than 47,000 postal and courier service points nationwide.

HKN2026 further recognised industry personnel through the Best Courier Worker award, the Safe Driving Challenge and the MyCSP Courier Safety Passport programme, with emphasis on safety and service quality. — Bernama
74ea1e5a8a953325: SEPANG: After a two-month injury lay-off, youngster Qabil Irfan Azlan made a sensational return to racing by winning race one of the Moto4 Asia Cup at the Sepang Circuit today.
Qabil crossed the finish line first in 27 minutes and 45.895s after fending off Indonesia's Bintang Pranata, who was just 0.166s adrift.
Qayyim Razali (+0.222s) made it a 1-3 finish for Malaysia on home soil.
Qabil suffered fractures to his left tibia and fibula during a crash in the Moto4 European Cup in Valencia earlier in September.
The 14-year-old said it felt special to win at Sepang after the challenges he has faced this season.

"I feel this victory is quite different and special because it came after I suffered an injury. I also have to be more careful to ensure my leg makes a full recovery, so this win means a lot to me," said Qabil.
"For tomorrow's race, I feel more motivated after winning today. Insya-Allah, I will try to put up another strong challenge and fight for the best possible result."
Sepang is currently hosting the fourth round of the Moto4 Asia Cup. Race two will be held tomorrow.
Qabil was forced to miss two rounds of the series due to his injuries.

a336ab677a302b8c: Microsoft senior software engineer Raymond Chen has explained what Windows is doing when you hold down the power button, and shared a story about the time a customer accidentally created a Goth Mode for Windows 3.1.

There's a section in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (actually, page 116 of this writer's dog-eared copy of The Restaurant at the End of the Universe) in which Zaphod Beeblebrox observes of a ship's interior: "Every time you operate one of these weird black controls that are labeled in black on black background, a little black light lights up black to let you know you've done it."
The same turned out to be true of a user who called Microsoft customer support to complain that after Windows 3.1 booted up, all that remained after the product logo disappeared was a blank screen.
It turned out the customer liked black a little too much and, according to Chen, made themself a Goth theme.

The customer support engineer on Microsoft's end pieced it together. The customer had, according to Chen, "set the wallpaper color to black. They set the title bar color to black. They set the button color to black. They set the window background color to black. They set the window text color to black.
"Every possible color you could pick in the Colors control panel was set to black."

We suspect the mouse pointer, at least, would have stuck around, unless the customer had also managed to change some settings around this. And then there are the icons… However, Windows 3.1 was a long time ago, and this writer's attempts at theming then were the consequences of growing up in the '70s and '80s, which resulted in some interesting neon, orange, and brown combinations.

As for Goth mode, Chen said, "Once you get yourself into this situation, it’s hard to get out because you can't see anything." One solution he suggested was deleting the [colors] section from the win.ini file.

Chen told the anecdote as a coda to the question – what exactly is modern Windows doing when you hold down the power button on a PC? According to Chen, after eight seconds of holding the power button, the Windows kernel realizes a forced power-off is happening and tries to take a kernel dump for diagnostics.

He explained that the kernel dumps were classified by Microsoft as "long power button hold" (LPBH) failures, with one of the bits of information captured indicating if all the pixels on the screen were black. The video driver might therefore be the culprit. Or whatever was responsible for drawing to the screen.
Today's Windows struggles with dark mode. But in the dim, distant past, every pixel being black might mean the user was either Hotblack Desiato or had done something very silly indeed. ®
cc45d95449db2b47: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will not resort to smear campaigns in the Melaka election, focusing instead on its candidates, service records, manifesto pledges and solutions for voters.
Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said voters should assess candidates based on their capabilities, experience and plans to take the state forward.

"We want to secure a mandate based on our own strengths, rather than by tearing others down. The people of Melaka deserve to make their choice based on facts, not slander or hatred," she said in a statement.
Azalina said candidates, party workers and supporters should campaign fairly, comply with election rules and avoid provocations involving race, religion and royalty.

She also called on Umno's information machinery, including its Wanita, Youth and Puteri wings, to strengthen digital campaigning, noting that 43.6 per cent of Melaka voters were aged between 21 and 40.

"Our communication approach must be more dynamic, creative and closer to young voters. Ensure that digital spaces are filled with accurate information, engaging content and factual, measured explanations," she said.
"Do not be easily influenced by unusually high numbers of likes, comments or shares. Check the sources, examine the facts and think before sharing."
Melaka's election campaign began today following nominations, with 79 candidates vying for all 28 state seats.
Polling is set for Nov 14, following a 14-day campaign period, while early voting is scheduled for Nov 10.

38811a1e540e2f78: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Stronger international cooperation is needed to address the global housing crisis, with approximately 3.4 billion people worldwide experiencing some form of inadequate housing, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.

In making the call, Nga, who is also United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly president, said that more than 1.16 billion people lived in informal settlements, including slums, while 44 per cent of urban renters spent an unsustainable proportion of their income on rent.

“Governments must ensure that housing is affordable, safe, well-connected to public transport and employment opportunities, and supported by essential public amenities,” he said in his keynote address at the opening ceremony of the Global Observance of World Cities Day 2026 in Fuzhou, China, today.

The event, themed “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, is jointly organised by UN-Habitat, China’s Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian Provincial People’s Government and the Fuzhou Municipal People’s Government.
Nga said addressing the crisis required more than building additional homes, as rising housing costs placed increasing pressure on households and widened social inequalities.
He urged governments, international organisations, and the private sector to strengthen partnerships in affordable housing, green development and sustainable urban regeneration.

Sharing Malaysia’s experience, Nga said the government had set a target of delivering one million affordable homes between 2026 and 2035, alongside an ambition to place Malaysia among the world’s top 10 countries for home ownership by 2035.

He highlighted the Malaysia Madani vision, the country’s housing reform agenda, and the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as key initiatives to improve housing accessibility and support sustainable urban development.
Nga also cited the RM60 billion Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), which facilitates access to home financing for 150,000 individuals without conventional income documentation.

“Housing is the foundational soil from which all human capability grows. It is where our children form their earliest ambitions, where working parents recharge their spirit, and where our senior citizens enjoy the honour they have earned over a lifetime.
“When a household enjoys a secure roof, every aspect of life stabilises. Health improves, educational outcomes soar, and economic confidence takes root,” he said.

Nga said a city’s success should be measured by the liveability of its neighbourhoods, the quality of public spaces, environmental protection and opportunities for residents, rather than merely its skyline or the scale of construction.

He said housing must cater to people’s needs from early childhood through to elderly care, while urban regeneration should support climate action through energy-efficient technologies and expanded green spaces.
Malaysia was also promoting transit-oriented development and climate-resilient urban renewal as part of its efforts to build more sustainable communities, he also said.

“Policy without execution is merely good intention, vision without action is only a dream,” he added, urging world leaders to translate international commitments into tangible improvements in people’s lives. — Bernama
7a38a0204b0efb2f: PETALING JAYA: Sarawak will push for greater control of its strategic resources, including the oil and gas industry, premier Abang Johari Openg said.

However, reclaiming such assets requires the backing of the people for the state government, he said. “The more Sarawakians stand behind us and our leadership, the more determined we will be to continue fighting for Sarawak,” Abang Johari was quoted as saying.

Abang Johari said Sarawak would not back down in its pursuit of oil and gas rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963. “We will not retreat. ‘Agi idup, agi ngelaban’,” he said, citing an Iban phrase that means to fight to the end.

In January, the Sarawak government officially took control of Bintulu port following the acquisition of a RM1.8 billion stake in the Bintulu Port Authority, which was previously under the jurisdiction of the federal government.
In 2024, Sarawak became the first state in Malaysia to own a bank, controlling a 31.25% stake in Affin Bank.
da773d195224100b: TEHRAN: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the US and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic's foes of a possible resumption of strikes.

"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
The war began on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader's statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US vice-president JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

f2beda2ca4bd0065: FRANKFURT, Oct 31 — German police were deployed across the country today and shops boarded up their windows ahead of protests that are set to draw tens of thousands of young demonstrators onto the streets.
Protest organisers “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) expect more than 170,000 people to turn out in over 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne.

The German demonstrations have been inspired by similar movements across Europe, including in France and Italy, which have seen young protesters voice anger at political elites whom they accuse of ignoring their concerns.

While “GenZ regelt!” stresses it rejects all violence, police are taking no chances and are deploying thousands of officers, while some luxury jewellery shops and clothing stores are boarding up their windows to ward off potential looters.

The protest movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation.
“The situation of young people is precarious, and yet they still aren’t being heard,” said Veronika Dinter, a spokeswoman for the movement.
“The institutions that are supposed to prepare young people for life are being starved of funds.”
They are also unhappy with sharply increased military spending and a new voluntary service model aimed at boosting troop numbers, fearing it is a step towards bringing back conscription.
Authorities are worried the protests, coinciding with Halloween, could be marred by the same kind of violence seen elsewhere in Europe.
Major protests are also expected in France on Saturday. Nationwide demonstrations there on October 17 degenerated into some of the country’s worst rioting in years.
Berlin is in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests.
But authorities say that they have not seen evidence of concrete plans for violence.
The “GenZ regelt!” movement meanwhile stresses that “extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism and hate speech have no place with us — no matter from which side”. — AFP
e5abfa83fcc1e009: KUALA LUMPUR: A congested fixtures and the national team's commitments have left the Malaysian Football League (MFL) with limited options in scheduling the FA Cup semi-final second leg between Kuching City and Selangor on Deepavali day on Nov 8.

The fixture at Stadium Taha Ariffin in Kuching has drawn concern from supporters celebrating the Hindu festival with their families. They may be unable to attend the match, which sees Selangor leading 2-1 from the first leg.
MFL chief executive officer Shazli Shaik said Kuching City's AFC Champions League Two (ACL 2) match against South Korea's Gangwon FC on Nov 5 was among the factors limiting the scheduling options.
The FIFA international window from Nov 9-17 further complicated matters, with the national team scheduled to begin their training camp after the FA Cup semi-final second legs.

"We have two teams, Kuching City and Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT), playing in their respective AFC Champions League competitions and the Asean Club Championship. They have additional matches to play, and this has forced us to fit the fixtures into the best available slots," he said.

"There are simply no other available slots for the FA Cup semi-final second legs. Kuching will play their ACL 2 match on Thursday and can only play 72 hours later in their return to domestic competition. MFL took into consideration of the match is being played in Kuching and if it's in Selangor the effects are more.
"MFL scheduled the FA Cup matches because only four clubs are involved, rather than the Super League, which would have involved more teams and made things more difficult for supporters.
"We also want to give Kuching a 72-hour break so their players can be in the best condition to perform in an important match."
Shazli said the national team's requirements also had to be considered, with preparations for the FIFA window beginning on Nov 9.
He stressed that the scheduling was not intended to disrespect the Indian community, adding that MFL had sought feedback from members of the community before settling on the arrangements.

"There is no intention on MFL's part to disrespect anyone, especially those celebrating Deepavali. We faced a similar situation last season with JDT and Selangor matches played during Thaipusam and we have previously held cup finals during festive celebrations. We now try to avoid that.
"We also checked with our friends in the Indian community and were informed that Deepavali prayers are usually held on the eve and morning of the festival.
"We hope fans can come and watch the matches at night with their family members after celebrating during the day," he said.
2bdae645524c8176: SEPANG: National Moto3 rider Hakim Danish Ramli continued his impressive progress at the Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (Moto3) by securing third place in today's qualifying session at the Sepang circuit.

1c5ea50414c198b3: LONDON: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was "open" to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.
The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean.
"I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today," Burnam wrote in the Guardian newspaper.
The transatlantic slave trade was a "brutal and barbaric violation" of the rights of those enslaved, he said.
The British premier added his government wanted a "structured dialogue with those affected."
"Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them."
The king is due to address the Commonwealth summit, which runs from November 1 to 4.
Britain's central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch's Caribbean tour.
In the Bahamas on Tuesday, Charles acknowledged "the great suffering of the past" during the first leg of his visit.
Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.
Burnham again rejected financial compensation, writing: "I do not believe that is the right answer."
"I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part."
Britain profited for centuries from colonialism and the slave trade. In 1833, parliament passed a law to abolish slavery.

818997468ee8972f: NAIROBI: The UN political mission in Somalia ended on Saturday after a two-year transition, closing a chapter of more than three decades of UN peacebuilding operations in the east African nation.

UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs.
It started as the UN Political Office for Somalia (UNPOS) in 1995.

In May 2024, Somalia's president Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.
During the transition, UNSOM was renamed the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS).

"Today is not an end to the partnership between the United Nations and Somalia – rather, it marks the conclusion of one chapter and the beginning of another," said Raisedon Zenenga, UNTMIS officer-in-charge and the UN secretary-general's deputy special representative for Somalia in a statement.
"While significant challenges remain, the closure of UNTMIS comes after considerable progress by Somalia since the early years of international efforts to support the country’s recovery," he added.
The mission's mandates have been transferred to either Somali institutions or the UN country team.

The transition comes as Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab, which has fought the Somali government for two decades, continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite a major international military campaign against it.

The fight against Al-Shabaab is increasingly threatened by international funding cuts, particularly after the United States withdrew all funding for a key UN logistics mission, casting doubt over the future of military operations.
Somalia is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections next May, with persistent insecurity and opposition disputes threatening the process.
1e7c9a7f0a873861: MUAR: Two women have been arrested following an incident involving a Muar Municipal Council enforcement officer during a stray dog-catching operation in a residential area yesterday.

447c99a74a473c6e: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government will not become poor or go bankrupt by helping the less fortunate, as the real threats to the country’s economy are misconduct among leaders, corruption and financial leakages, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

124eb8a4808f667b: Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it's the middle of the night while the clock says it's lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans.

A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions. And because these birds navigate by the Sun, that jet lag leaves a measurable mark—it skews their compass.

Patrick Lewin is a behavioral and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford and lead author of the study. “Manx shearwaters are medium-sized birds, about the same size as a pigeon,” Lewin said. “They are white underneath and black on top, but they have very long wings, and they are closely related to albatross.” Manx shearwaters nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic. Most breed around the UK and Ireland, with about half of their population living in Wales.
c94bd3c9fd5fe886: JOHOR BARU: The second day of the Jom Heboh Carnival (KHJ) Johor Baru 2026 at Angsana Johor Baru Mall here continued to draw large crowds today.

86d7a1194dd2b6ec: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government has allocated an additional grant of about RM200 million to strengthen the capacity of small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly those from low-income groups, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

f08b7bd38821897c: In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in. Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies?

493d74a6bcb2f43a: There's a ridiculously simple test you can use to figure out whether AI mandates at a given company are well-considered, or are being shoved out the door by out-of-touch buffoons: What happens when an engineer documents that AI made a task worse? Are they taken seriously, or are they marginalized and eventually managed out?

Conveniently, this week Amazon published a treatise by Terk Terkowitz, a VP/Distinguished Engineer/Final Boss of Their Independent Contributor Technical Career Track, on the role of the developer in the age of AI. It was originally an internal missive sent to their software engineers and their managers back in September, which is an interesting lag for a document that sounds this confident. It also maps exceedingly well to what other organizations are struggling with.

I think it's a good document, but I can't help but view it with a somewhat cynical eye. I see it as an attempt to make the future of the profession of software engineering feel less bleak. And it's feeling mighty bleak for a lot of folks right now.

This treatise comes at a time of dramatic upheaval. Tech as an industry is no stranger to change (usually at 3AM, heralded by the pager), but something about the current AI-ification of the world strikes many of us as fundamentally dissimilar from previous revolutions. Folks are scared about their career prospects. "Should I give up tech and get into farming?" is a sincere question multiple people have asked me. I don't know! Tech is already a goat rodeo, so you've got a leg up if you do?

This anxiety isn't theoretical. In May, Amazon wisely shut down KiroRank, an employee-built cash incineration leaderboard that ranked people by token usage, after the obvious thing happened: people spun up junk tasks to climb the ranks. This is now called "tokenmaxxing," and the Terkowitz treatise specifically calls it out as being at odds with "frugality." Meta did the same thing with "Claudenomics" and 85K employees that same week. And Amazon reportedly announced another 250 job cuts this week. I can't tell you that these things are related. But I can tell you that every engineer who read the memo assumes that they are.

This document contains a lot of great stuff. I have a tremendous level of respect, both personal and professional, for Amazon's Principal Engineering community; I'm led to understand that that respect may not be reciprocated, but that's okay. I am, by their standards, a lapsed engineer who ran away to join the circus as one of its lesser clowns.

Terkowitz's memo emphasizes customer outcomes and engineering judgement, two things I would absolutely not delegate to AI any time soon. (Note: I am writing this in October of 2026, with the full understanding that previous comments on the capabilities where AI falls short tend to age like fine milk.) It documents work that (today) AI tools aren't improving. That's way better than assuming that every objection to AI inherently comes from some self-interested Luddite who's scared of being replaced. It also says something smart about measurement: look at the 90th percentile of AI adoption, at those teams burning the most tokens, and check whether their delivery actually went up commensurately. This is great! Shout it from the rooftops; we should all be doing such things.

The memo says “If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing.” Document it, bring it to your manager, work through the problem. I agree with every word of that! The question is whether anyone's promo doc is gonna survive citing it.

Here's what happens next. The memo concedes that input metrics are "deeply flawed," but then in the next paragraph says to go ahead and use them anyway, carefully. It then warns that non-adopters are falling behind. Those are three different positions within three sentences and they're not at all aligned with one another.

That's not muddled; I think it's cover. A manager can cite "a finding, not a failing" when a strong engineer skips the AI tool, and then cite "falling behind" when it's time to PIP someone. Both are congruent with their stated policy; you get to decide which interpretation you want to go with in a given situation.

How will managers handle justified AI non-use? Are promotion and performance decisions being made in a way that rewards these long term outcomes? Or are they instead taking the easy weasel way out, optimizing for what's cheap to measure, and rewarding tool activity? Because if you give me a metric, I will turn it into a target. So will an overwhelming majority of employees. When that happens, everyone loses — it's how KiroRank happened in the first place.

I write this after two days of attending GitHub Universe, where they talked about how agents start roughly 40% of PRs now. And yet, Jay Parikh’s keynote argument was that useful output wasn't "more code," but rather completed outcomes: features shipped, bugs fixed, security issues addressed, loudmouth columnists silenced, etc. The problem here is that their entire business model cuts against that; they're billing in a model that charges customers on a consumption basis, not an output basis. There's nothing, today, that ties "AI spend" to "output that was worth the effort."

Which brings us back to Amazon. The memo says tokenmaxxing is at odds with frugality, and for Amazon’s internal cost line, it is. Meanwhile AWS bills Bedrock and Kiro customers by the token. Inside the building, tokenmaxxing is a problem to be stamped out. Outside it, it’s the revenue plan. ®

<!--kg-card-end: html--> Welcome back to the Abstract—and Happy Halloween! Here are the studies this week that smashed into Earth, put aliens on ice, drank mummy wine, and hugged it out.

First, a century-old theory that comets enriched Earth with the stuff of life is upended by new models of ancient impacts. Then: the case for life in extraterrestrial sea ice, a Halloween-coded medieval concoction, and a scientific embrace.
As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter The BeX Files.
Did the seeds of life come from above or below?
Anslow, Richard J. et al. “Cometary impacts are an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth.” Scientific Reports.

Carl Sagan eloquently said that we are all made of “star stuff,” but just how much of us is really comet vomit? This is a hotly debated question in science due to the popular theory that comets delivered essential ingredients for life to Earth during impacts more than four billion years ago, paving the way for the curious emergence of Earthlings.

But scientists have thrown cold primordial water on this idea in a new study that challenges “the long-held assumption that cometary impacts played an important role in the origins of life on Earth.” By running more than 100,000 advanced simulations of comet impacts, the team found that key prebiotic molecules found in comets, such as hydrogen cyanide, would be smashed to smithereens during impacts with Earth’s ancient surface in most cases.

Moreover, while Earth was pummeled by these snowballs during its youth—relatable!—this bombardment doesn’t neatly line up with the timeline of abiogenesis, the term of the origin of life. For these reasons, it’s much more likely that life assembled from earthly molecules that leaked out from our planet’s interior, according to the study.

“The most probable timing of successful cometary impact is in the early Hadean…more than 100 [million years] earlier than the estimated emergence of the last universal common ancestor (LUCA) at 4.2 [billion years ago],” said researchers led by Richard Anslow of the University of Cambridge.

“Taken together, the rapid decline in Earth’s cometary impact bombardment and the efficient destruction of fragile cometary organics indicate that the successful delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules was an exceedingly rare event,” the team added.

The researchers didn’t rule out the possibility altogether, but concluded that any impact that had a direct influence on abiogenesis would be an edge case. That said, comets might serve as prebiotic wellsprings on other planets, such as Mars, where key molecules might have faced better odds of survival upon impact due to the red planet's smaller mass and thin atmosphere.

“Mars would have been the more favourable target for the cometary delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules” which “strengthens the possibility that life could have emerged on Mars,” the study concluded.
In other news…
The tip of an alien iceberg
Barrier, Edouard et al “Sea Ice as an Origin of Life Location for Hycean and Ocean Worlds.” Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

While we’re on the topic of prebiotic feedstock molecules—a household conversation, no doubt—let’s speculate about their accumulation on weird exoplanets. In a new study, scientists suggest that these molecules might build up in sea ice on a variety of extraterrestrial ocean worlds, providing a pathway to the emergence of aliens.

“Water worlds with potential deep oceans are at the forefront of currently observable exoplanetary habitability,” said researchers led by Edouard Barrier of the University of Cambridge. “Here we outline a location where nutrients could be concentrated in sufficiently high quantities to make abiogenesis possible—at the interface between the open ocean and the surface ice shelf.”

The team studied the dynamics of sea ice on Earth, and modelled how similar features might form on a range of different exoplanets, including hypothetical “Hycean” planets. These are worlds more massive than Earth, but smaller than Neptune, making them part of the “sub-Neptune” class of exoplanets.

The results revealed mechanisms that “may plausibly provide concentrated chemical feedstock for prebiotic chemistry” on many of these exoplanets, suggesting they could be a substrate for the emergence of alien life. This “rich avenue of research…has the potential to significantly advance our understanding of aquaplanet habitability, and particularly to improve the prospects of abiogenesis on sub-Neptunes,” the team concluded.

What a week for the prebiotic feedstock beat! Taken together, these studies point to multiple onramps for life on worlds like Earth, Mars, exotic sub-Neptunes, and more, upping odds that life exists elsewhere in the universe—regardless of whether we ever find it.
Drink the mummy wine
Berger, Tim, and Naimi, Amira et al.“New molecular and historical evidence on ancient Egyptian embalming.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

To celebrate Halloween, here’s a trick and a treat all wrapped up in one delightfully grotesque story about mummies. Roughly 700 years ago, someone had the interesting idea of grinding up parts of Egyptian mummies, mixing the residue with wine or other liquids, and prescribing it as a medicinal elixir for people to drink.

This resulting product, known as Mumia vera aegyptiaca, circulated in Arabic and European markets for centuries, but its exact composition and pharmacology remain unclear. You know what that means: It’s time to do science on the medieval mummy cocktails.

Researchers analyzed historical Mumia vera products, mummified body parts, embalming residues, bandages, and two mummified skulls. The team discovered a wide range of formulas for this medicine, including one powdered product that appears to have been derived from a mummified head.

The results demonstrate that “an apparently uninformative powdered material can be chemically linked to a specific mummified head,” said researchers co-led by Tim Berger and Amira Naimi of Marburg University. “This study shows that linking historical texts, material culture, molecular composition, and bioactivity, can open new routes for decoding historical medicines and reconstructing the material biographies of human remains and museum objects.”

So if you are really committed to the spirit of this season, break out some Mumia vera aegyptiaca to pair with your Halloween candy and witches’ brew. Bottoms up—or more accurately: mummified-heads up.
Advances in hug science
Dueren, Anna Lena et al. “Why we hug: Individual differences predict emotional touch memories.” PLOS One.
What better way to close out this chilling spooky season than with the warm embrace of science? So come on, bring it in for a hug—or, in this case, roughly 15,000 of them.

Hugging is an incredibly common form of affection among humans, and even some other animals, including Halloween favorites like vampire bats. But little is known about “how individual differences shape the remembrance of such experiences,” according to a new study.

To fill this cuddly gap, scientists analyzed survey responses from 15,049 adult participants in the United Kingdom who were recruited in a public broadcasting campaign that included the BBC. The volunteers reported that their most memorable hugs were “for comfort, support, and understanding” and there was a noticeable gender split, as men were more likely to remember hugs that were “arousing” than women.

“Regarding hugs, men have shown different lateralisation and arm crossing patterns when hugging other men compared to women,” said researchers led by Anna Lena Dueren of the University of Bristol. “Furthermore, women were found to experience a stress buffering effect of hugs that was absent in men.”

And for anyone who considers themselves not a “hugger,” you are not alone. Plenty of participants expressed that they found hugs difficult or unpleasant. So whether you love bear hugs or cannot bear hugs, this study has something for you.
Thanks for reading! See you next week.

3a1ffe3869962ee1: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Floods in Kedah and Negeri Sembilan have fully subsided, with all three temporary relief centres (PPS) in the two states closed today, while the number of evacuees in Perak has declined.

In Negeri Sembilan, two relief centres in Kuala Pilah, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Undang Johol and Dewan Orang Ramai Dangi, which housed 87 evacuees from 35 families, were also closed at 4pm today following improved weather and the complete recession of floodwaters.

In Perak, the flood situation has also improved, with the number of evacuees at SK Titi Serong relief centre in Kerian declining to 25 from nine families, compared with 34 people from 12 families this morning.
The Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said in a statement that all evacuees from Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1 had been housed at the centre since Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain tonight in Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. — Bernama
