bab8118c89ce09de: KOTA BARU: Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Sungai Golok estuary project within a month to help mitigate flooding in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had had two rounds of discussions with the Thai government, including with its new prime minister, to expedite efforts to resolve the issue.
He said maintaining good relations with neighbouring countries was crucial to ensuring smooth cooperation, particularly in addressing cross-border issues and promoting peace.
"I have had discussions twice with Thailand, including with its new prime minister, to expedite the matter.
"This is why we need to maintain good relations with our neighbours to ensure that cooperation can proceed smoothly," he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here today.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Anwar said the project involved addressing erosion, as well as widening and deepening the river to improve water flow and reduce flooding.
He said resolving the issue at the Sungai Golok estuary would require close cooperation between the Malaysian and Thai governments.
"I hope we can finalise the matter within a month to reduce the impact of floods in Kelantan and southern Thailand," he said.
He also expressed appreciation to the Kelantan government, particularly the state secretary, for expediting the land acquisition process to facilitate the project.
Anwar said he hoped the initiative would usher in a new chapter of development for Rantau Panjang, which had been affected by recurring floods.
He said he would hold further discussions with the Thai government within the next month to ensure progress.
The prime minister was on a one-day working visit to Kelantan.
c0532676bcad2cad: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress Datin Lisa Surihani believes singer-actor Alif Satar played a key role in her invitation to perform the haj, calling the opportunity an unexpected blessing she holds dear.

​Lisa shared her reflections during an experience-sharing session today organised by haj and umrah agency Irkaz Travel, titled Kerana Dia Memanggil (Sebuah Perjalanan, Seribu Makna) Mekah, Aku Datang.
​While she had initially hoped to make the holy pilgrimage alongside her husband, director and musician Datuk Yusry Abdul Halim, Lisa eventually came to peace with their separate journeys.

​"At first, it was difficult because we had prayed and hoped to go together, but it did not happen. Nevertheless, when it comes to acts of worship such as haj and umrah, we must never leave Allah out of our considerations," she said.
​Lisa emphasised that Allah is the ultimate planner.
Being invited to the Holy Land, she explained, is not about waiting until you feel completely ready, but about seeking divine guidance and trusting that your path will be made easy.
​The pilgrimage also taught her the true meaning of tawakal (placing complete trust in Allah), especially when it comes to letting go of the need to control everything.
​"As women and household managers, we often feel that we are the ones organising everything. But there, we realise that ultimately, everything rests in Allah's hands," she said.
​As an ambassador for Irkaz Travel, Lisa encouraged anyone feeling unsure about taking the step not to let self-doubt hold them back.
​"If you feel hesitant or unsure, just proceed with your intention if it is meant for you, because Allah knows what is best for His servants," she said.
78864943ceda8ce0: PARIS, Oct 31 — France today braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, as shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
The demonstrations come in an increasingly febrile political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls.
President Emmanuel Macron this week said it was “not normal” for France to be in such a state of “turmoil” so close to a presidential election.
Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest.
The sound of a helicopter and the occasional siren could be heard in eastern Paris this morning.
More than 40 metro stations were to be closed in the capital and tram services were expected to be disrupted.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they expected street violence on a scale “comparable” to the unrest two weeks ago, when images of clashes, looted shops and public buildings set ablaze were broadcast around the world.

The protest movement, bringing together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
Similar youth-led demonstrations have been seen across Europe in recent weeks, with marches also planned on Saturday in Germany.
‘Halloween is not helping’
A police source pointed to “considerable nervousness” among the authorities.
“There is no reason to think this will go smoothly,” the source said.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France’s chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.
“Shopkeepers can’t wait for Saturday to be over,” Di Crescenzo told broadcaster France Inter.
“The information we have is that Halloween is not helping matters, because we’re going to have people wearing masks.”
Ahead of the protests, some shops and other businesses across France boarded up their storefronts.
“Behind these boards, there is neither power nor an enemy. Just a family and its work,” read a message scrawled in black across the plywood protecting a Paris business.
The interior minister has warned of a “very high risk of public disorder”, saying demonstrations would be allowed, but not in city centres.
‘Revolution’
The Paris police prefecture authorised only a march on the outskirts of the capital, even though protesters had sought to rally in central Paris.

In a ruling seen by AFP, France’s highest administrative court, the Conseil d’Etat, on Saturday overturned a lower court decision that had approved the route through central Paris proposed by organisers of the main demonstration.
Nunez said authorities had detected social media calls for Halloween gatherings this evening urging protesters to spark a “revolution”.
Some posts on social media called on people to dress up and gather for a “night of darkness”.
Nunez warned that protesters would not be allowed to wear masks concealing their faces.
On Friday, customers crowded into a costume shop in Paris, but manager Didier Jarsale said it was not his job to “ask every customer what they intend to do with what they buy.”
“We’re not here to act as police officers,” he said.
Security failures
Authorities have acknowledged security and intelligence failures that helped pave the way for the clashes, widespread looting and vandalism that erupted on October 17.
Since then, they have moved to reassert control by restricting demonstrations and imposing curfews in several cities.
A night-time curfew will be imposed in the Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods of Paris from 11pm to 6am today and tomorrow.
The unrest followed weeks of demonstrations by students campaigning for better school conditions.

On top of the cost-of-living protests, the country was last week shaken by a shooting that killed one person and wounded seven, including an 11-year-old girl, outside Paris. Most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds.
The attack has triggered rallies against the normalisation of racist hatred. — AFP
5e2d4d1cd7a0c6ca: LONDON, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Andy Burnham said today he was “open” to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.
The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean.
“I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today,” Burnam wrote in the Guardian newspaper.
The transatlantic slave trade was a “brutal and barbaric violation” of the rights of those enslaved, he said.
The British premier added his government wanted a “structured dialogue with those affected”.
“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them.”
The king is due to address the Commonwealth summit, which runs from November 1 to 4.
Britain’s central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch’s Caribbean tour.
In the Bahamas on Tuesday, Charles acknowledged “the great suffering of the past” during the first leg of his visit.
Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.
Burnham again rejected financial compensation, writing: “I do not believe that is the right answer.”
“I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part.”
Britain profited for centuries from colonialism and the slave trade. In 1833, parliament passed a law to abolish slavery. — AFP

83f3029aab1fd9f2: TEHRAN: Iran's army warned Saturday that any new US attack would only spread their war wider, following threats by America and Israel of further military action as they hold crucial elections.

The Iranian warning comes with fresh diplomatic efforts underway to avert a resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators in Tehran and US vice-president JD Vance reportedly sending a letter to Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei.

"If the US president once again embarks on more regional adventurism under pressure from, and in an attempt to appease, the Zionists, the flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area," Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said in a post on X, without elaborating.
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi also warned on Saturday that "Iran's powerful armed forces will deal against those who dare harm our people."
On Friday, a Qatari delegation arrived in the Iranian capital for talks with senior Iranian officials.
Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran's security chief at the direction of President Donald Trump in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.
Iran has confirmed receiving the letter but has not announced any response.
The US holds midterm elections on Tuesday that could determine the direction of the war, which has proven unpopular with American voters following a spike in energy prices due to the conflict.
Last Tuesday, Israel also held legislative elections, with voters given a chance to offer a verdict on right-wing prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Under Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran's government, Israel and Iran have engaged in direct military confrontations after decades of shadow war.
The Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran that killed the country's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as well as senior military commanders.
Iran, in response, targeted US assets across the Middle East as well as Israel.
Most recently hostilities have focused on the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial Gulf shipping route for energy exports that Iran has blockaded since the start of the war.
The US has, in retaliation, been blockading Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the nation's economy.

36161bb06473615e: KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother.
“We do not know yet, which is why counsellors play a very important role. The Health Ministry also needs to involve the doctors and nurses handling the case.

“I cannot comment beyond what we know so far, as the police are still investigating the case, but our protection team is working with the family and counsellors to determine the actual problem so that they can provide assistance,” she told a press conference after officiating the KPWKM Santuni Kasih Programme here today.

Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.
She also advised mothers in need of emotional and postnatal health support to seek assistance through the MamaCare initiative, managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN).
Earlier, Kapit police chief DSP Rohana Nanu was reported as saying that a baby boy who was still alive was found buried in the ground near a rented house in Jalan Airport, Kapit, on Wednesday.

The baby, who was initially reported to be in critical condition, was rushed to Sibu Hospital for specialist treatment, while the case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
08485332045d3a97: PETALING JAYA: PAS's Mata Ayer assemblyman, Wan Badariah Wan Saad, has died at the age of 50.
In a Facebook post, Perlis PAS said Wan Badariah breathed her last at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah in Kangar at 4.26pm today.
In May 2024, she was placed in an induced coma after suffering heart and lung complications, and spent about a month in intensive care before being moved to a normal ward and discharged.
Wan Badariah, a shariah lawyer, was elected Mata Ayer assemblyman in 2022, defeating her rivals from Umno and PKR with a majority of 2,021 votes.
She was a member of the Perlis executive council under the Shukri Ramli administration, overseeing the women, family, community development, tourism, welfare, and disaster relief portfolios.
4b412aaeef5fe371: PETALING JAYA: The poultry processing plant in Puchong raided by authorities on Thursday is found to have electrocuted chickens to death before processing them for distribution.
The Selangor Islamic religious council (Mais) said an investigation found that the plant used electric water baths to stun the chickens, but the electrical voltage used was too high.
This instantly killed the birds when they were dunked into the water before being slaughtered in accordance with Islamic law, Bernama reported.
"This means they were essentially slaughtering carcasses rather than live chickens, as required under Islamic teachings," said Mais chairman Salehuddin Saidin.
Salehuddin said a preliminary investigation found that the slaughterhouse, which has been operating since 2004, was owned by a Muslim and supplied processed chicken to Muslim-owned restaurants.
"This is a highly irresponsible act, and we will ensure that firm action is taken. The company has been operating for a long time, more than 20 years.
"I am, therefore, rather perplexed as to how something like this could happen, and why they would so easily deceive Muslims when they themselves are Muslims," he said.
Following the raid, the authorities ordered the plant to close for two weeks under health regulations, to allow for further investigation.
Salehuddin urged eatery operators supplied by the firm to stop using its chickens immediately.

"I urge Muslims, restaurant operators and food business owners to check the source of their chicken supplies, in particular, as they must ensure that the food they serve is suitable for consumption by Muslims," he said.
A multi-agency operation led to the raid, during which 12 foreign workers were arrested and more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken seized.
A preliminary investigation indicated that the premises sourced its chickens from several poultry farms around Sepang.
The processed chickens were believed to have been distributed to restaurants, grocery shops and supermarkets across the Klang Valley.

Dozens of police guarded the building as followers of the opposition right-wing Law and Justice party (PiS) protested what they called an attempt by prime minister Donald Tusk's government to seize control of the institution.
The court's official X account said there had been a "coup d'etat" and some demonstrators chanted "Tusk traitor" and tried to push through security barricades. Police said three people were arrested.
Tusk was "trampling on our constitutional rights", demonstrator Tomasz Zaleski told AFP outside the court.
US ambassador to Poland, Tom Rose, warned all sides: "Don't take any action that could provoke violence or further escalation."
"The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse," he said on X, adding the country a friend and ally of the US while voicing concern for its stability.
Tusk's government has been trying for weeks to force out the court's judges, who were appointed by the previous PiS government that ruled from 2015 to 2023.
The court frequently ruled in favour of Polish legislation over EU law, and the EU accused Poland's highest court of being too close to the nationalist political power of the time.
Mid-flight chaos

Tusk, a strongly pro-EU figure, vowed to end the dispute with Brussels after winning an election in 2023. But the country's president, a right-wing independent, has blocked his nominations to the court.
Former PiS prime minister Jaroslaw Kaczynski addressed the demonstration and called for Nawrocki to act.
The president, who was travelling to Senegal for the opening of the Youth Olympic Games, ordered his plane to return to Warsaw.
Back in the capital, Nawrocki met with Swieczkowski and the court's first chief justice Zbigniew Kapinski before heading to the court, according to his chief of staff Pawel Szefernaker.
Nawrocki pushed his way through the crowds to enter the building, local TV footage showed.
The suspension of Swieczkowski was announced by another judge, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who said the move was needed to restore the rule of law.
Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek, who is also the attorney general, told journalists he had requested the lifting of the legal immunity of Swieczkowski and his deputy, Bartlomiej Sochanski.
"This court has become private property; we must restore its proper functioning," he added.
Tusk justified the action on X, saying, "Restoring the rule of law is our duty."
"After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way."
Adding to the confusion, the court's X account insisted Swieczkowski remained in office.
Korwin-Piotrowska could not become interim chief, as she had not been sworn in by the president, it added.

da437b2cdfcd45f0: PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage.

“I do not want to say to make it compulsory, but we must encourage them. Perhaps the Information Department, before issuing the annual media accreditation card, could ask if they have undergone a medical check-up,” he said today.

He said this in his speech at the launch of the Journalists’ Health Screening Programme with the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation ahead of the 2026 MMC Annual General Meeting here.

Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.

Fahmi later told reporters that the proposal for media practitioners to undergo annual health screening has not been set as a prerequisite for media card holders, adding that it would be discussed with the MMC in detail first.

“We will discuss this with the Media Council (and) with all media companies to assess its feasibility; for instance, if this initiative involves facilities in the Klang Valley, it may pose some difficulties for our colleagues in Sabah and Sarawak, or in areas outside the Klang Valley.
“We do not intend to make it compulsory, but we would like to encourage all media teams to undergo health screenings at least once a year. That is our intention,” he said.

On today’s programme, he said the RM1 million initiative, contributed by ECM Libra Foundation to the CVSKL Foundation, aimed to help improve access to preventive healthcare services, particularly for active and former journalists.

“We view problems involving the health of journalists as one of the key issues. These screenings can help identify non-communicable diseases at an early stage, allowing us to provide assistance earlier and help prevent any untoward incidents from occurring,” he added. — Bernama
87474b5d923226bc: PETALING JAYA: Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) dan Majlis Paralimpik Malaysia (MPM) bekerjasama untuk meningkatkan kesedaran masyarakat terhadap keterangkuman golongan orang kurang upaya (OKU) menerusi inisiatif '#WeThe15: Inclusive Together'.

cccccd681779cc0e: Today's bit of signage silage is either Windows 10 protesting that it is not part of London's Oxford Street pedestrianization, or someone failing to heed an alert before the public is made all too aware that things aren't going well…

Eagle-eyed Register reader Aaron Colwill spotted the sign outside the food hall entrance of a Marks & Spencer store on London's Oxford Street. It usually entices passersby through the doors with promises of treats inside, but today it appears to require a different kind of feeding. Disk space is running low.

Marks and Spencer (also known as M&S and Marks and Sparks) is no stranger to cyber whoopsies, having been the victim of an attack in 2025 in which crooks made off with customer data. Later that year, it reckoned cleanup costs would be about £136 million.
That's quite a lot, but not enough to buy a bigger hard disk for Windows 10, it seems. Storage prices have increased over the years, but surely not that much?

Colwill reckoned that Windows 10 21H2 LTSC was behind the problems. It could well be. While support for 21H2 ended for many users in 2023, Windows 10 LTSC 2021 will carry on until Jan 12, 2027, meaning engineers might have an exciting festive period ahead of them. Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC 2021 will receive extended support until Jan 13, 2032.
Either way, using Windows to advertise the Food Hall's wares seems slightly overkill. Simple posters, for example, never run out of disk space or attract the bork fairy's attention.

Perhaps they might use something that lacks the voracious appetite for storage that Microsoft's finest demands. According to the Windows biz, installing Windows 10 requires at least 32 GB of disk space, ideally more. It all seems a bit excessive for a cake-based caterpillar advert. Then again, when your operating system tends to have the resilience of a chocolate teapot, using it to advertise a chocolate insect might not be such a bad idea after all. ®

d27b8284b36d94fe: Nvidia is more than just a leader in graphics and AI hardware. It has also become a titan of the networking industry with bigger datacenter Ethernet sales than any other vendor.
In Q2, Nvidia's networking revenues topped $17.5 billion. To put that in perspective, Cisco's revenue during that same period, across all products, was $17.3 billion.
GPUzilla's arrival as a networking power feels sudden, yet Jensen Huang started working towards this status in 2019 with the $6.9 billion acquisition of long-time networking partner Mellanox .

At the time, Mellanox wasn't a big name in Ethernet switching. The company was mostly known for its ConnectX NICs and InfiniBand switches. Outside of high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing clusters, and a big deployment at Microsoft, InfiniBand wasn't widely deployed in hyperscale datacenters.

Buying Mellanox allowed Nvidia to reposition itself as a system builder, which means something different in the context of distributed compute. Nvidia understood its datacenter customers weren't interested in buying GPUs or even servers; they wanted clusters of systems. For that, Nvidia needed interconnect and Mellanox's InfiniBand fit the bill.
Relentless co-design

Over the years, Huang has talked about co-design – designing components and software to work together for specific set of jobs rather than to be the best GPU, switch, or NIC. Its work with Mellanox is a prime example of that approach.
According to Dell'Oro Group analyst Sameh Boujelbene, Nvidia's decision to integrate compute and networking became key to the company's success.

"Customers choose Nvidia for its tightly integrated compute and networking architecture, optimized for AI workloads," she told The Register. That integration makes deployments easier and speeds time to market.
Ben Mabey, CTO of pioneering AI and machine learning company Recursion, told The Reg Nvidia's integration schemes won him over.
Founded in 2013, nearly a decade before ChatGPT made AI the subject of dinner-table discussion, Recursion sought to apply machine learning running atop GPUs to the problem of drug discovery.
This work involved churning through massive datasets which, Mabey tells us, now total more than 50 petabytes in size.
"When you think about our workloads, it makes LLMs workload training seem easy compared to the amount of data that has to be moved around," he told The Register.

"In the biological space and sciences in general, it's not well appreciated just how big the data actually is," he added. "The internet's big, but in the grand scheme of things, the text that people are training on is actually pretty small, versus the petabytes of data that we have of these images."

Recursion's first cluster was a system called BioHive Zero which it cobbled together from GTX 1080 graphics cards originally intended for gaming systems. It used Ethernet to connect GPUs and ran into the limits of conventional networking.
So, for its second cluster, an A100-based machine with around 300 accelerators, Recursion went with Nvidia's Quantum InfiniBand switches and ConnectX NICs.

As Mabey explains it, buying its compute and interconnects from the same vendor vastly simplified optimization and troubleshooting. When Recursion reached out to Nvidia for help tuning the system, they were able to consider it as a single system, rather than discrete compute and networking resources. This level of integration had only previously been offered by boutique supercomputer builders like Cray or Atos (Eviden/Bull/whatever it gets renamed next).
A wider Spectrum
Nvidia hasn't always listed networking revenue as a single line item in its financials. However, based on CFO commentary and a little back of the napkin math we can fill in the blanks.
Nvidia's networking revenues have grown steadily since the Mellanox acquisition. At two moments, its revenue shot up suddenly.
The first came in the 2023 calendar year (FY24) after OpenAI kicked off the AI gold rush with the launch of ChatGPT.
The second spread across 2024 and 2025, when Nvidia started selling Blackwell-generation GPUs and then started to ship them in large quantities.

"I see two major inflection points, both coinciding with the Blackwell platform ramp: the introduction of NVLink switches and the accelerating adoption of Spectrum-X Ethernet switches for AI back-end networks, driven by growing deployments of Nvidia GPU clusters and increased attach rates of Nvidia switches, NICs, optics, and cables," Boujelbene said.
It was around this time that users started deploy to Ethernet switches in large volume across Nvidia clusters. Elon Musk's Colossus supercomputer was one of the earliest examples.

As we reported at the time, the first half of the 200,000-chip H100 and H200-based cluster came online in 2024 and, at the time, was among the largest ever clusters deployed using Nvidia's Spectrum-X Ethernet switches.
Meta has also made extensive use of Nvidia's Spectrum switches in its own training clusters, including at its million-GPU Prometheus site in New Albany, Ohio.
There are a couple reasons Nvidia's Spectrum-X offering is doing so well.

First, through a combination of Spectrum Ethernet switches, superNICs, and some clever software optimizations, Nvidia was able to replicate many of the qualities that made InfiniBand so attractive while also benefiting from significantly higher radix and interoperability.
Ethernet switches, including Nvidia's own, have historically offered more ports. The higher the radix, the fewer switches are necessary to support a cluster at a given port speed.

This often gets misconstrued to mean that InfiniBand can't scale beyond clusters of a certain size, which isn't necessarily the case. But for clusters exceeding a certain number of GPUs, Ethernet is often more economical because it requires less equipment while achieving similar utilization.
That said, Nvidia's Spectrum-X isn't exactly unique. Broadcom, Cisco, AMD and others have managed to achieve utilization similar to InfiniBand through various investments in smartNICs and switches.
Nvidia's main differentiator, as Mabey and Boujelbene noted earlier, is the level of integration between the compute and networking.
The next frontier
Then Blackwell hit the market, enabling much greater scale and creating a surge in Nvidia's networking revenue.

Prior to Blackwell, Nvidia's NVLink and NVSwitch interconnect tech had largely been limited to single systems with up to eight GPUs. With the launch of the GB200 NVL72, these NVSwitches were broken out into dedicated appliances. (And yes, we remember GH200 NVL256 and NVL32, but from what we can tell these were never shipped in any meaningful volume, if at all.)

For every NVL72 rack system sold, Nvidia also sold nine NVSwitch trays, which enabled the system's six dozen GPUs to function as a single enormous GPU. This effectively guaranteed steady networking revenue growth: even if customers didn't buy Nvidia's scale-out switches, if they wanted NVL72 racks, they were automatically buying NVSwitch.

"We estimate that NVSwitch now accounts for roughly one-third of Nvidia’s networking revenue, up from virtually zero less than two years ago," Boujelbene told El Reg. "This underscores how quickly NVLink switching has become a major growth engine for Nvidia’s networking business."
Nvidia is now moving to grow its networking business even further with a new licensing program.

Until recently, Nvidia's NVSwitch tech was limited to its own accelerators. However, with the introduction of NVLink Fusion early last year, Nvidia opened the interconnect tech up to third parties to license.

Many chip designers, including Marvell, Qualcomm, Arm, Fujitsu, MediaTek, and d-Matrix, have announced plans to develop CPUs and XPUs using NVLink Fusion. The adoption of the interconnect opens the door to additional NVSwitch sales, as the chips using NVLink Fusion still rely on them for chip-to-chip communications, and there's no other place to get them, as Nvidia has yet to license out NVSwitch.

"NVLink Fusion allows Nvidia to extend its networking footprint beyond its own GPUs into the rapidly growing custom accelerator market. I see it as a strategic move to capture a larger share of AI networking spending, even in clusters that do not use Nvidia GPUs," Boujelbene said.
Nvidia's networking ambitions don't stop there.

"Nvidia continues to pursue opportunities in emerging networking domains as network requirements evolve to keep pace with increasingly demanding AI workloads," Boujelbene added. "The latest example is scale-in networking, designed to address the new requirements of agentic AI, while innovations such as CPO will help overcome growing bandwidth, power, and scalability challenges." ®

6d6ace8f977196fc: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 31 — OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being scraped to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every bot that crawls the web to collect data, but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that’s recognised and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out “in the coming months,” while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has “already started” rolling it out.
The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

In December 2023, the Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft for allegedly using millions of its articles without authorisation or payment to train ChatGPT. The two tech companies are invoking an exception to copyright law known as fair use.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content scraping will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher’s content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

“We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry,” Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort. — AFP

6f2278fea9c4ba0b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A primarily US-owned startup is planning a US$600 million (RM2.4 billion) investment in a Malaysian rare-earth refinery, aiming to develop a new critical minerals supply chain as Washington moves to reduce its reliance on China.

DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology expects to establish the facility within three years, chief executive officer Milan Perlly said in an interview. The startup recently became the first company to receive permission under Malaysia’s relaxed export regulations to ship unprocessed rare-earth material to the US, Bloomberg reported.
“The larger goal is to make Malaysia the rare-earth elements processing hub for ionic clay in the region,” Perlly said.

Much of Malaysia’s identified rare-earth wealth lies in ion-adsorption clay deposits. These elements bind loosely to clay rather than locking into hard rock, making extraction cheaper and more efficient. Crucially, they contain the heavy rare earths vital for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and advanced military technology.
DTEC Mineral plans an initial processing capacity of 5,000 tonnes annually. The company ultimately envisions two facilities in Malaysia with a combined output of 10,000 tonnes a year.
“The US wants us to build 10,000 metric tons output,” he said. “My goal is to put one plant on the east coast for 5,000 metric tons, a second plant on the west coast.”

Perlly noted the firm is evaluating sites after holding discussions with state officials in Kedah, Terengganu, Perak, and Negeri Sembilan. These new facilities would expand Malaysia’s rare-earth footprint beyond the existing Pahang operations run by Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd.

Moving forward, DTEC Mineral intends to develop locally sourced ionic-clay deposits and eventually operate its own mine. While government data places Malaysia's rare-earth resources at an estimated 16.1 million tonnes, much of this remains commercially unproven.
To determine the most suitable processing technology, the company is preparing to ship 30 tonnes of unprocessed material to the US for research, having secured approval to export up to 700 tonnes.

Perlly, a Malaysian-born US citizen and former Capital One executive, holds a 51 per cent stake in DTEC Mineral alongside business partner David Greer. Local firm DTEC Engineering and Construction owns the remaining 49 per cent.
The startup harbours ambitions for a dual listing on Bursa Malaysia and either the Nasdaq or New York Stock Exchange.
DTEC was part of a critical minerals pact signed between US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last year.

According to the company's website, the agreement makes DTEC eligible for funding from the Export-Import Bank of the United States, the US International Development Finance Corporation, and the Department of Defense.
1fb4bfe9bce21a7a: BEIJING: China's factory activity slipped back into contraction territory in October, official data showed Saturday, despite sustained growth in high-tech industries, as the market for consumer goods weakened.
The manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI), a closely watched gauge of industrial health, came in at 49.3 this month, below the 50 mark separating expansion from contraction.

The fall in manufacturing activity was in part driven by a week-long national holiday at the start of the month, as well as a "complex and volatile international environment", according to NBS statistician Huo Lihui.
The figure, from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), missed the forecast of 49.9 by a Bloomberg survey of economists and was below the 50.1 and 49.8 recorded in September and August respectively
However, it was above the 49.2 recorded in July.
Prices for international crude oil have continued to climb, hiking up the prices of coal, rubber and plastic products, Huo said.

Despite "positive development momentum" within the high-tech sector fuelling the artificial intelligence boom, the PMI for the consumer goods industry in October was down 1.9 percentage points from the previous month, showing that "market activity has somewhat weakened", he added.
Beijing is hoping for annual growth this year of 4.5 to 5.0 percent, its lowest goal in decades, as sluggish domestic demand weighs on its export strength.
"Strong exports alone are not enough to boost the economic momentum," said Zhiwei Zhang, chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management.
"If the external demand weakens in 2027, China will need more significant policy support to boost domestic demand," he added.
The non-manufacturing PMI, which measures activity in other areas including services and construction, came in at 49.7 in October, the data showed.
That was lower than a Bloomberg forecast of 50.0, and down from the 50.2 recorded in September.

Huo, the NBS statistician, said the drop was "influenced by factors such as a decline in (business) prosperity within certain service sectors," particularly the financial sector, but did not elaborate.
There was also a slowdown in construction activity compared to the previous month, Huo said.

a7412ad3d096dc27: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s brother has stressed the urgent need for transparency in the domestic equity market, warning that Jakarta must “mitigate the MSCI issue” and demanding that corporate leaders immediately stop “deep frying” stocks.

“I’ve been tasked by the president to help ensure this doesn’t spiral out of control,” Hashim Djojohadikusumo said in Jakarta, speaking in his capacity as the president’s special envoy and advisory board chairman of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Kadin), according to Bloomberg.

“This is a very, very serious issue,” Hashim said. “Because if foreign investment pulls out of our stock market, the rupiah could weaken further. We’ll have to pay more for our foreign loans. This could become a disaster and catastrophe for the Indonesian economy.”

US index compiler MSCI Inc warned earlier this month that Indonesia could face a downgrade to standalone status, a severe sanction triggered by mounting concerns over opaque shareholding structures and coordinated trading in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
The warnings have hammered sentiment on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, where the benchmark index has tumbled roughly 41 per cent this year, weighed down by a 3.5 per cent slide on Thursday.

In response to MSCI’s October 15 notice, Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority (OJK) announced penalties against more than a dozen entities involved in market manipulation. OJK head Friderica Widyasari Dewi confirmed on the sidelines of the Kadin forum that sanctioned firms have since paid IDR2.1 trillion (RM512 million) in fines, though the regulator has yet to disclose their identities.

Hashim addressed an audience comprising hundreds of business figures, including tycoons Anindya Bakrie and Franky Widjaja. Widjaja is the ultimate controlling shareholder of PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa, one of the entities under regulatory scrutiny.
His warning came days after President Prabowo asserted that “the Indonesian nation is not afraid of anyone and will not be intimidated.”
Hashim pressed market players to halt the local equivalent of saham gorengan, the coordinated churning and ramping of share prices detached from corporate fundamentals.

“Please stop deep frying stocks immediately because the government intends to take firm action,” Hashim said, cautioning that capital outflows triggered by a potential double downgrade could push the rupiah to 22,000 per US dollar. “This would have an extraordinarily negative political impact.”

Bank Indonesia Governor Destry Damayanti told reporters at the gathering that currency fluctuations reflect multiple dynamics, including global market sentiment. She noted that the central bank remains focused on ensuring currency stability to support real-sector expansion, emphasising that the rupiah is backed by solid underlying fundamentals.
Hashim added that the protracted equity slump directly hurts retail investors across the archipelago.

“There are 32.7 million Indonesian citizens who hold brokerage accounts — in other words, they’re investing through the stock market,” he said. “Well, the problem is that right now, those 32.7 million Indonesians are extremely dissatisfied with the situation. They’re unhappy because the value of their stocks has dropped.”
Hashim, an established conglomerate head who has long served as Prabowo’s key financial and political strategist, played a pivotal role in backing his brother’s path to the presidency.

64c205aac7cf6354: PARIS, Oct 31 — Global anti-money laundering watchdog the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) said Friday it had removed Monaco and three other countries from its “grey list”, two years after it put the principality among its territories requiring increased monitoring.
Bulgaria, Democratic Republic of Congo and the Ivory Coast were also removed from the list, the organisation said after a plenary meeting.
The countries had completed promised action plans “and will no longer be subject to the FATF’s increased monitoring process,” it added.
The Paris-based FATF monitors efforts by more than 200 countries and jurisdictions to prevent money laundering and the financing of terrorism.
Grey list nations are considered to have “strategic deficiencies” in countering money laundering and terrorist financing, while cooperating with the FATF to correct the problems.

Long known as a playground for the rich and famous, tiny Monaco, with a population of less than 40,000, attracts moneyed residents from around the world with its extremely favourable tax regime, with no income or wealth taxes.
The FATF said Monaco had made “significant progress” in strengthening the effectiveness of its efforts to counter money laundering and terrorist financing.

“This decision recognizes more than two years of concrete, rigorous and coordinated work by all of the State’s authorities and departments,” the head of Monaco’s government, Christophe Mirmand, said in a statement.
The FATF had urged the Mediterranean principality to boost resources for investigators and prosecutors and increase seizures of property suspected to derive from criminal activities.
It called for more effective cooperation on countering money laundering and terrorist financing, and for officials to send more requests to identify and seek the seizure of criminal assets abroad.
Monaco introduced an offence of presumed money laundering to facilitate the prosecution of cases involving suspicious funds.
It also boosted funding for its financial regulator and created a special unit in the public prosecutor’s office.
“We do not see this as a finish line: what matters now is what Monaco delivers over the long term,” Mirmand added.
Dozens of money-laundering probes were underway in 2025, and convictions rose from three in 2021 to 28 in 2025, according to Monaco’s authorities.
Bulgaria, which had been put on the grey list in 2023, also welcomed its removal.
This “means more confidence in our country, more investment and more jobs,” Prime Minister Roumen Radev said in a statement.
It will also facilitate Bulgaria’s international financial transfers, he added.
Democratic Republic of Congo had been on the grey list since 2022 and Ivory Coast since 2024.
The exit of the four countries leaves 18 on the FATF’s grey list, including Bosnia, Bolivia, Iraq, Syria, Yemen and the British Virgin islands.
Three countries are on the FATF’s black list of countries that are high risk for money laundering and terrorism financing: Iran, Myanmar and North Korea. — AFP

7d73457714d933a5: LONDON, Oct 31 — Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, estimates that assets worth US$6.3 billion (RM25.7 billion) were impacted by a hacking attack against the trading platform.
But how was such a theft possible, and what does it reveal about the security of cryptocurrencies? AFP takes a look.
Is Binance reliable?
Binance, the world’s largest platform by digital currency trading volume, claims to have 335 million users.
That compares to the reported 741 million cryptocurrency owners worldwide cited by Crypto.com.

However, Binance has faced its fair share of scandals. Its former CEO, Changpeng Zhao, was convicted in the United States in 2024 for violating anti-money laundering laws, though he was later pardoned by President Donald Trump.
It has faced further US legal troubles, including being accused of selling assets that qualify as unregistered securities.
In France, Binance is suspected of having failed to meet its obligations regarding the oversight of client funds.
Having failed to obtain authorisation under the European Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) regulation, Binance recently announced a partial suspension of its operations within the European Union.
A secure technology?
Cryptocurrencies are based on a technology called blockchain, a digital ledger that records transactions and is designed to make falsification particularly difficult.
Transfers are authorised using “private keys” – long strings of characters kept secret. However, this does not fully protect funds from theft.
“Even when you think you are using one of the most robust exchanges in the world, it can still be hacked,” Stephane Ifrah, an analyst at Coinhouse, told AFP.
How can hackers still get in?
To gain access to private keys or the systems that authorise transfers, hackers can exploit a software vulnerability, deploy malicious software, or target individuals – for instance through phishing.
Some keys are stored on hardware wallets that are not connected to the internet.
However, these devices are not immune to attacks. Funds belonging to users of the French firm Ledger were stolen after malicious components were inserted into devices sold by a third-party retailer.
In the case of Binance, the investigation is pointing toward a “compromised” laptop of one of its engineers, in addition to “points of breach”, the platform said on X.
Who are the hackers?

While there has been no official confirmation, analyst firms TRM Labs, Chainalysis and Elliptic point to hackers linked to North Korea, specifically the group known as TraderTraitor or the “Lazarus Group”.
The amount purportedly stolen is four times the sum that the same hackers – according to the FBI – siphoned from the platform Bybit in February 2025.
That theft totalled US$1.5 billion, which at the time was the largest ever cryptocurrency heist.

According to Elliptic and Chainalysis, some of the funds stolen from Binance have been traced to the same pool of assets as those taken in a recent hack of the platform Bitget, which the victim attributed to Pyongyang.
Is it possible to recover the money?
Binance says that around US$3 billion of the affected crypto – nearly half the total amount affected – has been frozen with help from issuers and infrastructure partners.
But the freezing of assets does not mean the funds have been recovered.
According to Ifrah, the attackers could employ anonymisation tools, such as cryptocurrency “mixers” or “tumblers”, designed to make tracking the stolen assets more difficult.
Binance asserts that it will cover the losses resulting from the hack.
But as Ifrah states, “it is clear that there is no such thing as zero risk”. — AFP
ad44b28d5894c3f0: PARIS, Oct 31 — The Fitch ratings agency on Friday maintained France’s credit rating at A+ but downgraded its outlook from “stable” to “negative” as it raised new concerns over the cost of paying for the country’s debt mountain.

The US agency predicted that the debt level for the European Union’s second biggest economy would rise from nearly 115.7 per cent of GDP in 2025 to 124 per cent in 2028. Its last review in August had forecast that France’s debt would reach 122.7 per cent of GDP in 2028.

“Weaker growth, renewed fiscal deterioration and higher yields have increased the challenge of delivering the necessary sustained fiscal consolidation to arrest France’s worsening debt trajectory,” it said.
International investors have expressed widespread concern over France’s debt level and this has pushed up the interest yields it pays to service debt, which is one of the highest in Europe.
The country will hold a two-round presidential election in April-May next year, and Fitch said the prospects for debt reduction after the vote were “uncertain”.
It said the political divisions, with far-right and far-left candidates leading opinion poll surveys, would make it difficult to agree “a credible fiscal strategy”.

“The emerging policy debate ahead of the presidential election has not materially strengthened Fitch’s confidence in the prospects for durable deficit reduction that could lead to debt stabilization. Large protests over public services and living costs further complicate the social context for fiscal consolidation,” it commented.
The Fitch assessment came after the INSEE national statistics agency reported Friday that the economy has not grown so far this year and contracted in the period from July to September.
The government is also struggling to get parliament to pass its budget, aiming for a reduction in spending, for 2027. This has compounded market fears.
“If we fail to achieve the turnaround outlined in the budget, we are headed straight for a wall,” Finance Minister Roland Lescure warned in a radio interview. — AFP

Shares in Google’s parent company Alphabet fell a further 1.8 per cent after heavy selling Thursday that wiped billions of euros off its value.
Wall Street’s tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index fell 2.7 per cent in midday trading.
“It is unlikely that the AI trade will recover on Friday, and instead the focus is shifting to the non-tech sectors of the market and safe havens,” Brooks said.

Focus is turning also to Tuesday’s US midterm elections and the impact they could have on the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

Shares in ExxonMobil rose 1.9 per cent after it reported that its third-quarter profits more than doubled to US$15.4 billion on higher oil prices and refining margins due to the US-Iran war.
Elsewhere, bitcoin fell five per cent to US$77,167 after trading platform Binance said it had fallen victim to a major hacking attack that had hit around US$6.3 billion in funds.
That is four times the amount involved in the previous biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, which saw US$1.5 billion taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform. — AFP
8f9e81279e5a8c4d: From Moaz Nair
If you ever feel ignored at work, underappreciated by your friends or are generally invisible to the human eye, take comfort. You could be the Malaysian Indian People’s Party (MIPP) or Gerakan.
In the grand corporate hierarchy of Perikatan Nasional (PN), these two are the interns who don't get invited to the lunch table, yet somehow believe they are next in line for the CEO's position.
To say that MIPP and Gerakan bring no clout to PN is a profound insult to the word clout.

They are the political equivalents of plastic indoor plants – supposed to add a splash of "multiracial colour" to a very green room – except the plants have withered, the owners keep forgetting to water them and the landlords are currently trying to evict the entire building.

The political future of these minority component parties in PN has become one of the most ironic talking points in modern Malaysian politics. Critics, political analysts and observers frequently debate their position, although "debate" might be too active a word. It is more akin to watching two passengers argue over who gets the window seat on a bus that has already driven off a cliff.
MIPP: from bold newcomers to zero-vote club

Let’s start with MIPP, the bold newcomers whose political future in PN is currently the hottest topic among three guys at a coffee shop. MIPP entered the scene with the explosive energy of a damp firecracker. At its grand electoral debut in Johor, it contested five seats and managed a spectacular, flawless clean sweep of losing their deposits in all five.

MIPP’s standing within a major coalition remains precarious precisely because it has demonstrated a rare, mathematically impressive lack of an independent base. Yet, MIPP’s confidence remains unshaken by minor details like numerical reality.

Recently, the party announced it would completely sit out the Nov 14 Melaka state election after seat distribution talks with the PN leadership broke down. The official reason? President P Punithan bravely declared that the party refuses to compromise its dignity or accept "irrelevant" seats just to field candidates.

Translation: PN offered it a constituency consisting entirely of three palm trees and a stray cat, and MIPP chose "dignity" over another hefty loss of deposit. This breakdown signals deep friction over how minority component parties are treated by the dominant Malay-Muslim parties in PN.

The ideological mismatch here is staggering. MIPP is trying to pitch a minority-interest narrative in a coalition heavily dominated by PAS’s religious and conservative Malay narratives. It’s like trying to sell vegan burgers at a Texas steakhouse and acting surprised when the chef throws a spatula at you. It is incredibly difficult for a minority-interest party like MIPP to gain genuine traction among non-Muslim voters while standing next to politicians who view secularism as a design flaw.

Ultimately, MIPP’s decision to bypass Melaka highlights the ongoing, tragicomic struggle for minor non-Malay component parties to find an equal voice in a house that doesn't even know they are in the room.
Gerakan: master of the secular submissive

Then we have Gerakan, the veteran master of political irrelevance. The argument that Gerakan has no future in PN is a view increasingly shared by political analysts, critics, and even internal party factions who have grown tired of buying antacids in bulk.

Political observers highlight several compounding crises that threaten Gerakan's long-term viability in the coalition. First and foremost is its utter inability to attract non-Malay voters. Gerakan originally joined PN to serve as its non-Malay face, a bridge to the cynical urban electorate. Instead, it has become a cautionary tale, repeatedly failing to win over non-Malay voters from Pakatan Harapan, particularly DAP.

This has trapped it in the "shadow dilemma" – a polite academic term for operating entirely in the shadow of its larger partners, PAS and Bersatu. Because Gerakan brings minimal electoral data or seat victories to the table, its leverage in PN is roughly equivalent to a discount voucher that expired during the Asian financial crisis.

The ideological friction between Gerakan’s secular principles and PAS’s Islamic stance peaked hilariously during the school brewery donation saga. When PAS attacked the fund-raising, Gerakan deputy president Oh Tong Keong threatened to exit the coalition over "extreme" demands. PAS responded with a collective yawn, and Gerakan naturally stayed – proving that its red lines are drawn in invisible ink.

Naturally, this masterclass in political submission has triggered an internal rebellion. High-profile departures – such as the resignation of 31-year veteran and party treasurer Hng Chee Wey – underscore a growing internal revolt against sacrificing core principles for political expediency. These exits expose deep cracks under president Dominic Lau, as grassroots members grow tired of watching their leadership nod politely while being publicly sidelined.
PN's burning house

To make matters funnier, the house that Gerakan and MIPP are clinging to is literally on fire. The broader PN coalition is undergoing severe structural shocks, with PAS announcing the end of its political cooperation with Bersatu, triggering a chaotic power struggle and the sudden resignation of top PN leadership.

The Registrar of Societies even ordered the coalition's deregistration, and while a temporary court reprieve saved it from legal oblivion, persistent internal rifts cloud the bloc's political future. It is a civil war where the big boys are throwing live grenades, and Gerakan and MIPP are caught in the crossfire armed with plastic cutlery.

What is Gerakan’s next move? Political analysts suggest that leaving the coalition may be a risk worth taking compared to staying and enduring further humiliation. Yet, Lau has indicated that Gerakan is trying to pivot by backing a broader PN-Barisan Nasional electoral tie-up for future stability.

Yes, you read that correctly. While PN is on the verge of structural collapse and PAS is actively exploring independent realignments with Umno, Gerakan is trying to build a bridge to a party that doesn't know it exists, using a blueprint that is already out of date.
Conclusion

Gerakan risks being completely left behind unless it thoroughly recalibrates its political alignment. But that would require a sense of direction, and right now, both Gerakan and MIPP seem perfectly content to sit in the back seat of a driverless car heading straight towards a cliff, arguing over who gets to hold the auxiliary cable.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

2286dcf6a47eca45: NEW YORK, Oct 31 — Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a “complex attack” that affected around US$6.3 billion (RM25.7b) in funds, in what is thought to be the biggest ever crypto heist, with investigators pointing to hackers linked to North Korea.

Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said it had “high confidence” that the attack was orchestrated by a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor, the same group blamed for the US$1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.
Another analytics firm, Elliptic, also attributed the attack to North Korea-linked hackers, according to industry outlet CoinDesk.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, said investigations had “uncovered additional points of breach,” contrary to initial findings that suggested the hack involved a single compromised laptop.
“This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance wrote on X.

The company confirmed on its X account for Latin America that “the total estimated impact is around US$6.3 billion,” four times the amount taken in the Bybit hack, the biggest cyberattack of its kind until now.

Binance warned the figure “may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.”
It said around US$3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.
Customers’ account balances have not been touched, but they cannot move funds off the platform while withdrawals remain suspended.
Binance initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals but later said deposits were unaffected. At about 0900 GMT Friday, it said it was on track to resume withdrawals in 45 hours.

President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was “engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity” and was ready to investigate.
Fund freeze

The company had said on X that initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a “DevOps engineer,” allowing the unauthorized party to execute unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
“We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets,” it said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete.
The unauthorized withdrawals drained Binance’s hot wallets – the online wallets the exchange uses to process customer transfers – across several blockchains, according to CoinDesk.
Binance earlier posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages, insisting that “user funds are completely safe” but also saying it would “cover all losses.”
Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether, a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT, said his firm froze about US$1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.”
Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than US$800 million in USDC.
USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.
Crypto prices tumble
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.
The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, except for the stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins.
Bitcoin plunged nearly five per cent after the news, falling overnight to around US$76,400, its lowest level since mid-September, before recovering slightly to trade at about US$77,300.
Ethereum dropped nearly six per cent, while BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 per cent.

The attack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. — AFP

68f2fe60ad7543ba: Washington’s decision to order non-emergency American diplomatic personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia is more than a precautionary measure. It signals a dangerous deterioration in the security environment of West Asia.
For Malaysia, the implications are immediate, strategic and potentially costly.

Saudi Arabia is not merely another oil-producing country. It is a pivotal power in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), the custodian of Islam’s two holiest cities and an indispensable pillar of global energy security.
When Washington begins withdrawing diplomatic personnel from Riyadh, Kuala Lumpur must pay attention.
The decision follows increasingly audacious attacks by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi airports, energy installations and civilian infrastructure.
The recent targeting of Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport and Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield demonstrates how asymmetric warfare can undermine even a militarily sophisticated state.

Saudi Arabia possesses advanced Western weapons systems, extensive financial resources and powerful international partnerships. Yet relatively inexpensive drones and missiles continue to penetrate or challenge its defensive arrangements.
This carries five important lessons for Malaysia.
First, energy security cannot be separated from national security.
Although Malaysia produces petroleum and natural gas, its economy remains vulnerable to disruptions in global energy markets.
Higher transportation costs, expensive imported industrial inputs and renewed inflationary pressures could weaken domestic purchasing power.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s unity government has worked to preserve economic stability amid considerable international uncertainty.
A prolonged crisis in Saudi Arabia could undermine these efforts, especially if disruptions spread across the Persian Gulf and Red Sea.
Second, maritime security must be understood as an interconnected strategic system.
The Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb are indispensable arteries of international commerce.
If both become increasingly dangerous, shipping companies will face higher insurance premiums, longer journeys and mounting operational costs.
Malaysia, strategically positioned along the Strait of Malacca, cannot remain insulated from these developments.
Disruptions in West Asia can eventually affect Malaysian ports, manufacturers, exporters and consumers.
Third, the Houthis have demonstrated the growing effectiveness of asymmetric warfare.
Military superiority no longer guarantees comprehensive security.
Drones, missiles, cyberattacks and sabotage can inflict enormous economic damage without requiring conventional military parity.
Malaysia and Asean must therefore strengthen the protection of airports, ports, energy installations and communications networks.
The strategic lesson is straightforward: resilience matters as much as deterrence.
Fourth, Saudi instability carries serious implications for Malaysian pilgrims.
Mecca and Madinah remain central to the religious lives of Malaysian Muslims.
Any deterioration in aviation security or airport operations could complicate haj and umrah arrangements.
Wisma Putra, Tabung Haji and Malaysia’s diplomatic missions must strengthen contingency planning, particularly regarding evacuation procedures, flight disruptions and consular assistance.
The safety of Malaysian citizens must remain paramount.
Fifth, the American decision exposes the limitations of excessive dependence on external security guarantees.

The United States remains militarily formidable. Nevertheless, its decision to reduce diplomatic exposure demonstrates that even Washington cannot eliminate every security threat confronting its allies.
Malaysia must therefore deepen its strategic relationships with Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan, China and other influential powers.
